newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Fruit and vegetables push up NZ FPI in October.
newsitem.headline: Fruit and vegetables push up NZ FPI in October.

text.p: Fruit and vegetable prices, which rose 0.8 percent, were the main contributor to the 0.4 percent rise in the New Zealand Food Price Index in October, Statistics New Zealand said on Wednesday.
The index rose 3.2 percent in the October year against a 3.1 percent rise in the September year.
The fruit group rose for the first time since December mainly due to higher potato, cabbage, pumpkin and tomato prices.
The other major contributor to October's price rise was increased grocery costs of 0.5 percent. Soft drinks, sugar and artificial sweeteners are credited as driving the rise.
Restaurant meals and ready-to-eat food recorded a 0.3 percent increase in the month.
The only sub-group to post a fall was meat, fish and poultry, where prices fell 0.4 percent mainly due to falls in mince, steak and pork prices.
Prices rose 0.4 percent in the North Island and 0.3 percent in the South Island.
